clue.text: Unfinished model drum

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a pattern is a model to copy

explanation.surface: A half-built toy drum sits on the workbench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts the last letter from PATTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a steady rapid tapping, as of rain on a roof.

clue.text: Left gap somewhere in ship

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a hole is a gap or opening

explanation.surface: A gap left somewhere on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A porthole is a round window in the side of a ship, so a place found in one.

clue.text: Match underground scientific apparatus

parts.note: a test is a cricket match, a Test match
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Science kit is taken by Tube to a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is a small glass cylinder used in laboratory work.

clue.text: Support revised lease

indicators.note: revised means the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant backs an amended rental agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painting or blackboard.

clue.text: Almost sin having a tantrum in minister's home

indicators.note: almost the whole word means its last letter is left off

parts.note: a vice is a sin or moral failing
a tantrum is a fit of rage

explanation.surface: A cleric's house is the scene of a near-sinful outburst of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a Church of England minister, and the house provided for one is the vicarage.

clue.text: Popular cereal dye

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
grain is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A trendy breakfast cereal is coloured with dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrain is a dye fixed into fibres before weaving, a fast colour worked in deep.

clue.text: Pleasant feelings following good base

parts.note: after means following
base means low or mean in character

explanation.surface: Warm feelings come after a solid foundation is laid.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterglow is the warm contentment left after a happy experience.

clue.text: Makes suitable commercial appropriate to go on top of scoreboard

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
apt means appropriate

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An advert is fitted to sit atop the scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to change it so it fits a purpose, making it suitable.

clue.text: Greek letter to church after European Union employee found in harem

indicators.note: after places the Greek letter and church behind the union's letters

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is sent to church after an EU worker is found in a harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A eunuch was a castrated man employed to guard the women's quarters of a palace.

clue.text: Fantastically shrewd to keep vacated land

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the emptied word goes within

parts.note: wily means shrewd or cunning

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cunning landlord fantastically keeps an empty plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties a word down to its first and last letters; 'to keep' holds the result within the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildly and fantastically both mean extravagantly, beyond all reason.

clue.text: Opposing cheat after one's queen returns

indicators.note: after places the cheat behind the reversed pieces in the answer
returns means the pair of pieces before it is read backwards

parts.note: one's read as 'one is', the I standing for one, giving IS
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the queen
a sting is a confidence trick, a cheat

explanation.surface: Someone resists a swindle once the queen comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', with I for one; 'returns' turns the queen and that pair round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Resisting something is opposing it; both describe pushing back against a force.

clue.text: Prepare for starvation regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the next word is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: An athlete gets ready for a period of going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of 'starvation' give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to prepare oneself or someone else through practice and instruction.

clue.text: Somewhere to stay following golf?

definitions.meaning: a place offering rooms to travellers for the night
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the word for H comes straight after Golf, the word for G

explanation.surface: A golfer wonders where to spend the night after a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf' looks like the sport but is the NATO alphabet word for G.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a commercial lodging house, and in radio spelling it is the code word that follows Golf.

clue.text: Mark day institute gets a judge

parts.note: a critic is one who judges or assesses work

explanation.surface: A school's judge hands out marks on results day.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is a mark such as an accent or cedilla added to a letter to change its sound.

clue.text: Balance on line in public building

parts.note: Libra, the zodiac sign, is represented by a pair of scales or balance
RY, short for railway, stands for a line in crosswords

explanation.surface: Scales are set on a line inside a town building.
explanation.definitionFit: A lending library is a classic public building where books are kept for borrowing.

clue.text: Sees hula dancing around old pubs

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go about the next piece
dancing means the letters of the words move about

explanation.surface: Someone watches a hula performed in old taverns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges SEESHULA into ALEHUSES; 'around' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a tavern or pub serving beer.

clue.text: River having nothing to East

parts.note: nil means nothing, as in a football score

explanation.surface: A river that has nothing to the east of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa, flowing north through Egypt.

clue.text: Note jam is socially acceptable in pudding

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to jam is to ram or cram
U means upper class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A notice says jam is fine in the dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge layered with mascarpone.

clue.text: Smokers caught by that man with noisy joints

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
him refers to that man

indicators.note: noisy means the next word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: knees are joints of the leg

explanation.surface: Smokers are caught by a man whose joints creak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisy' asks for the sound of KNEES, spelt NEYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimneys give off smoke, so playfully they are smokers.

clue.text: Setter with small cat cries

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as ME
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: The setter and a small cat are crying together.
explanation.definitionFit: A mew is the high thin call a cat makes, so the plural gives its cries.

clue.text: Part of grist or a germ in silo?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Grain and germ are kept together in a silo.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower for keeping grain, so what happens in one is keeping in reserve.

clue.text: Sentimental old lady having desire to embrace king

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, MA

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so the king goes inside the desire

parts.note: a wish is a desire
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A soppy mother longs to hug the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lady' is slang for one's mother; 'to embrace' wraps the desire around the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly sentimental, cloyingly emotional in a way that embarrasses.

clue.text: Heads of media in Russia request operational reports for news outlet

indicators.note: Heads of means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Media chiefs in Russia ask for working reports for the news.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mirror is a British daily tabloid newspaper, a news outlet.

clue.text: Pig's home the Parisian designs

parts.note: a sty is where a pig lives
les is French for the, in the plural

explanation.surface: A Paris designer lays out a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Styles are designs or fashions, as in different styles of dress.

clue.text: Register for jobseeker's allowance in song unusually

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone claims unemployment benefit by breaking into song.
explanation.walkthrough: Jobseeker's Allowance was the UK unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain to sign on is the idiom for registering as unemployed to claim benefit.

clue.text: Flag excursion around Rhode Island with colonel

indicators.note: around says the trip wraps about the next pieces

parts.note: a tour is an excursion or trip
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
COL is the military abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A colonel tours Rhode Island waving a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' has the excursion wrap the state and the officer, which sit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a flag of three bands of colour, such as the French or Irish national flag.

clue.text: Jerk springs on top of mountain

parts.note: spas are mineral springs

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word, in a down-the-page sense its head

explanation.surface: A sudden movement sends water springing up on a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is an involuntary jerk or twitch of a muscle.

clue.text: Grimace of bird squashed by Special Constable

indicators.note: squashed by places the bird hard up behind the constable's letters

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for a Special Constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird pulls a face when a police volunteer sits on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashed by' sets OWL tight against SC; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl is an angry frown, a type of grimace.

clue.text: Briefly closes eyes having lost black ties

indicators.note: having lost means the letter for black is removed from the word

parts.note: one blinks by shutting the eyes for an instant
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone shuts their eyes for a moment after losing a black tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' belongs to the eye phrase, not a truncation signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are connections or bonds between things, so ties in that sense.

clue.text: Eat humble pie made from a loose pig

indicators.note: made from means the following letters are reworked to form the answer

explanation.surface: A humble pie made from a pig that escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat humble pie is an idiom for admitting one was wrong and saying sorry.

clue.text: Left home carried by nun

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the following word

parts.note: a nun is addressed as Sister
in means at home

explanation.surface: A nun is left holding the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb in the surface but is the definition; 'carried by' puts home inside the nun's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is the Latin and heraldic word for left, as opposed to dexter for right.

clue.text: Obscures flash covered up by civil service

indicators.note: covered up by means wrapped inside the following letters

parts.note: flash, as an adjective, means showy or loud

explanation.surface: A flashy scandal is hushed up by civil servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flash' is the adjective meaning showy; 'covered up by' sets it between the civil service letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud something is to make it dim or unclear, to obscure it.
